about: MateEngine    MateEngine  is a lightweight, customizable desktop companion app that brings 3D anime-style characters to life on your screen. Built with VRM model support, it allows you to inject your own avatars and watch them interact, idle, and even dance—right from your desktop.    This project is a alternative aimed at giving users more control and flexibility without relying on expensive model packs or locked-down systems. Whether you want a simple virtual presence or a more animated character hanging out while you work, MateEngine is designed to be approachable and performance-friendly. To use custom models, you must download them from websites that offer .vrm files, or commission artists who create or convert models to the VRM format.  I am not responsible for the quality of third-party models. If you experience clipping or similar issues, the model's author is responsible, not this app.       RELAXE ON WINDOWS           Drag your pet onto a window and it will relax on top! Perfect for watching videos she'll watch with you. Or let her quietly spy while you do your homework, hehe.   This feature is experimental and not fully developed. Please avoid using it with apps that have anti-cheat protection enabled.    DANCING           She will start dancing when you play music! You can decide which apps are allowed to trigger dancing.  Open the Options menu, go to the audio sources, and whitelist your music apps.   Tip:  Start the music app first (e.g. Spotify), then open the menu and add it to the source list!     HEAD AND SPINE MOVEMENT           Not just the head — her eyes, head, and spine all follow your mouse cursor!  This makes the movement look smooth and natural compared to other desktop pets.     HAND MOVEMENT           Careful! Sometimes she’ll try to grab your mouse — hehe!  Move your cursor near her hands or arms and watch her try to catch it!     TOUCH REGIONS           Hover your mouse over sensitive areas like the head or belly to trigger cute gestures!  For example, hovering over her head makes her giggle and spawn sparkle effects, making her feel comfy.     CHATTING           You can chat with your pet anytime! Just note that it’s a small, local AI with simple messages.  For more complex conversations, you can use mods with your own models and messages!     RELAXING           When you drag her to the taskbar, she’ll lay down and relax on a big candy macaron, watching your mouse cursor with sleepy eyes.     DRAGGING           You can reposition her by clicking and dragging her with your mouse.  Just hold the button down and move her wherever you like!     CHIBI MODE           Hold your mouse over her feet for a few seconds and she’ll transform into a tiny,  adorable chibi version of herself — extra smol and cute!   CUSTOMIZATIONS           You can change her size, animation speed, language, and modes.  There are also graphics and FPS settings for low-end (potato) PCs!   DARK MODE           You can turn off lighting — perfect for VRM models with emissive textures!  Pair it with the glow/bloom toggle and your pet will shine like a diamond in the dark   MODDING           Modding is supported! Load your own VRM model by pressing the VRM button. If your model doesn’t load, it’s likely corrupted or not exported correctly. Make sure to export using the correct format:     VRM0.X : Uses  MToon Shader      VRM1.X : Uses  MToon10 Shader  Also make sure your model uses a proper humanoid bone setup. short: A hundred chess games on Steam. One of them gives you 40 AI opponents up to 2550 Elo, live open lobbies, async play, a league mode, a mini board that sits on your desktop and lessons that turn beginners into threats. You already know which one this is.
about: Most chess apps teach you the basics and leave you hanging. Most chess games are fun but won't make you better. Chess Kingdom does both. Whether you've never touched a chess board or you're looking for your next real challenge, this is where you grow.   START ANYWHERE. KEEP IMPROVING.   Six structured training campaigns take you from absolute beginner to advanced player, each focused on a specific part of the game. Piece movement. Tactics. Openings. Middlegame strategy. Endgames. Deep calculation. Hand-crafted lessons and puzzles, carefully ordered so every concept builds on the last. No guessing what to study next. No jumping in the deep end. Just clear, satisfying progress with star ratings, XP, and titles to show for it.       CLIMB THE LEAGUE   League Mode is a football-style division system with 6 tiers, from Wooden Shield to Diamond Crown. Play a full season against the AI opponents in your division. Finish 1st to promote. Finish last and face relegation. Earn trophies, collect stars, and climb your way to the top. Win Division 1 and you unlock a 2-game showdown against Phantom, the hidden League Champion. Can you claim the crown?       THEN COMES THE REAL TEST   Training and League are just the beginning. Chess Kingdom gives you every reason to keep playing.    40 AI opponents, each with a distinct personality, playstyle, and country. From Daisy the friendly beginner to Titan the ruthless master, and two secret opponents to unlock.    Tournaments. Single Elimination, Round Robin, Swiss. Climb a bracket. Prove your ranking.    Elimination Mode. Win or go home. One loss ends your run. How far can you get?    Async Online Multiplayer. Challenge friends via Steam and make your move whenever you're ready. No need to be online at the same time.    Daily Puzzles and Puzzle Rush. Stay sharp every day.    Play Kung Fu Chess: a real-time mode where both players move at the same time with no turns, or go Extreme and earn buffs, unlock power tiers, and unleash double moves by playing aggressively.    Atomic Chess: a tactical new variant where every capture detonates a 3×3 explosion, kings can't capture, and blowing up the enemy king wins the game instantly.    Game Analysis. See exactly where you won or lost, move by move.         MAKE IT YOURS   Choose your country from more then 40 nations, each with a unique piece set inspired by that country's culture and art. Indian Mughal pieces. Japanese Shogi-influenced designs. Dutch Delft-style boards. Your flag in your profile. Your style on the board. Unlock more as you level up through 100 player levels: piece sets, board themes, backgrounds, and titles earned through real progress.       BUILT TO GROW WITH YOU   Chess Kingdom is built by a solo developer using AI-assisted development, which means faster updates, more content, and the ability to act quickly on what the community asks for. New country skins, training content, and features are added regularly. Your feedback directly shapes what comes next.       ONE GAME. EVERY LEVEL.   Chess Kingdom grows with you. The beginner finishing their first lesson and the player grinding League Mode for the Diamond Crown are playing the same game, just a different chapter of it. The board is set. How far will you go?

about: Desktop Companion is the most powerful AI companion that lives on your desktop: an always-on-top avatar that sees your screen, works the live web, and remembers every conversation, building a real relationship over time. Not another AI chatbot stuck in a browser tab, but a real on-screen presence, always one glance away. Everything runs on your own machine, right out of the box: no account, no key, no setup.     Before you buy: hardware requirements   Desktop Companion runs entirely locally on your own PC (or on another machine on your local network). It requires a recent  dedicated graphics card with at least 10 GB of VRAM ; 12 GB or more is recommended. Integrated graphics, found in most thin laptops, are not supported.  Results may vary depending on your hardware and the model you use.      It lives on top of everything   Your companion floats above every window (games, apps, browsers), always one glance away. A real desktop presence, not a tab you alt-tab to.     It doesn't just answer, it acts   Ask for something and it goes and does it. It searches the live web and reads real pages, so it answers with today's information instead of stale training data, with nothing to sign up for and nothing to configure. It tracks what's blowing up on Reddit and X, checks the weather, and opens your apps and your folders. And when there's something worth keeping, it writes the file itself: a quick note, a Word document, a full spreadsheet, saved and ready to open. One request, and the work is done.     It sees your screen   Show it anything on screen and it reads it straight from a screenshot: a game, a chart, a line of code, a menu in another language. Point it at a chess position and it'll walk you through your next move. Screen vision runs on the built-in model, on your own graphics card, so what's on your screen stays on your machine.     Your Twitch co-host   Connect your Twitch account in one click and your companion joins your stream as a live AI co-host: it reads your chat and replies to your viewers in character, out loud, with moderation controls you set. Bring your own VTuber model and never stream to dead air again.     It remembers you   Real long-term memory. It keeps what matters from your conversations and brings it back days later. Close it, come back, and it picks up exactly where you left off.     It runs entirely on your machine   Desktop Companion comes with its own AI model, built in and ready the moment it's installed. Nothing to download, no account to create, no key to paste, no credits to buy, no monthly bill. Every reply is generated on your own graphics card, and your conversations stay on your machine. Unplug the network cable and it keeps working exactly the same. One purchase, and it's yours.     It speaks, and you can clone a voice   Three text-to-speech engines are included and run side by side, all of them local and free: Pocket-TTS, Kokoro and OmniVoice. Clone a voice on your own machine and give every character its own: in high quality with OmniVoice, or on the CPU alone with Pocket-TTS. Nothing is sent anywhere. Live captions show every spoken line in the language you choose, so it can speak one language while you read along in another. Switch on Anime Mode and it speaks real Japanese with subtitles on screen.     Nine characters, or build your own   Start in seconds with nine hand-written personalities, each a fully scripted persona localized into all 8 languages: Anna the Playful Sibling, Alice the Witty Historian, Michael the Gaming Buddy, Amelia the Supportive Friend, Mei the Yandere Girlfriend, Rei the Calm Mentor, Iris the Tsundere Companion, Lyra the Creative Muse, and Marc the Stoic Coach. about: An idle MMO in the corner of your screen Lowbar Legends runs in a small card in the corner of your screen, above the Windows taskbar. Pick a task, like chopping yew logs or fighting bears, and your character keeps doing it until you pick something else. Close the game and the task keeps going for 12 hours (24 with the Premium Charter). When you come back, you see what you got.         What you do    14 skills, up to level 120.  Woodcutting, Mining, Fishing and Foraging gather. Carpentry, Smithing, Cooking, Alchemy and Enchanting turn that into planks, bars, food, potions and runes. Melee, Ranged, Magic and Slaying fight. Excavation digs, and the dig sites change every week.   Running a task around the clock, level 99 takes about two months and level 120 about a year.    5 bosses , from level 60 to 116. Fight them with any combat style, collect each boss's weapon set and upgrade it to +10. Upgrades never fail.    6 achievement diaries  with 5 tiers each. Finished tiers give chests, a pet and lasting perks such as longer offline time.   Mastery Capes at 120, a pet for every skill, a collection log and leaderboards.         Every drop trades on Steam There is no auction house in the game. To sell something, send it to your Steam inventory with the Caravan and list it on the Steam Community Market like any other Steam item. Resources, gear, Vault Keys, chests, dyes, skins and pets can all be sold. What you buy on the Market comes back into the game through Arrivals. Mastery Capes and diary rewards stay on your account. As with every Market sale, part of the price goes to Steam and part to the game. Rare drops keep the name of the player who found them.         Clans A clan holds up to 50 players. Train the same skill as a clanmate and you both get a little more xp. Give materials to clan projects, like the Clan Wharf or the Hunting Grounds, and every member keeps the bonus once it is built. Each week the clan fills the Sunken Vault raid together, and it pays out on Sunday. Upgrading the clan hall gives every member up to 12% more xp. Free to play There are no ads and no energy bars. The Shop sells two optional items:    Premium Charter:  24 hours of offline progress instead of 12, up to 2 backup tasks that take over when your task runs out of materials, 3 Caravan slots instead of 1, Enchanting and Alchemy past level 30, and your name in gold on boards, clan lists and chat.    Patron:  looks only, for players who want to support the game. Pick one of 6 chat name colors, and get a ◆ mark and a Patron tag next to your name.  Both are items. Use one yourself or sell it on the Steam Community Market, so a player who never pays can still buy a Charter from another player with what they have sold. There is no PvP. Xp, items and upgrades never depend on luck; the only random drops are pets, chests and cosmetics.  Report bugs from the ? menu in the game window.

about: Bring Reimu to your desktop   Your Reimu  is a desktop companion who shares your daily life with Hakurei Reimu from Touhou Project.  Leave Reimu in a corner of your screen while you work. Now and then she'll mutter to herself, greet you when you come back after a while, and tell you something different on special days.  Indifferent and blunt, but she stays by your side in her own way.  Click, lift, and move her around  Click Reimu and she'll react with a line of dialogue. Keep clicking over and over and she might grumble that you're being a pain.  Press and hold to lift Reimu up and move her wherever you like. She sways and tilts as she follows your cursor, then settles naturally wherever you let go.  You can also resize her with the mouse wheel, and her position and size are kept even after you restart the app.  Leave your to-dos with Reimu  Put a simple TODO list on your desktop to jot down what you need to get done.  Add tasks, check off the ones you've finished, or delete the ones you don't need. Reimu reacts each time you knock one out, and when you clear the whole list she'll acknowledge your effort, saying you've earned a little rest today.  “Got one done. Not bad, actually.”  Timers and alarms too  When you need to focus, start a timer right away or enter any duration you like. You can also set an alarm to go off at a specific time.  One minute before the timer ends, Reimu lets you know it's time to wrap up, and when time's up she nudges you herself along with an alert sound.  “I'll watch the clock. You just do your thing.”  The TODO list and alarm widgets can each be opened separately and moved wherever you like.  Never in the way, but always there  Areas without Reimu or a widget stay clickable, so she won't get in the way of other programs. Talk to her only when you feel like it, or open the TODO list and alarm when you need them.  Less of a secretary who does the work for you, more of a housemate who watches from the side and chimes in now and then.  Spend your days with Reimu—blunt, allergic to hassle, and fond of a good donation. [hr][/hr]  月影工房 Work No. 7    This game is a fan-made derivative work of Touhou Project by Team Shanghai Alice. about: How a run plays  A red-hooded archer with a silver moon bow holds a road the horde never stops pouring down. She fights on her own; what she becomes is up to you.     Every kill pays.  Gold buys upgrades, level-ups give perks, bosses drop eggs and gear.     Hit a wall? Ascend.  Trade the run for relics that boost everything for good, keep your pets and gear, and go farther next time.     She never stops shooting.  Leave the game on a second monitor, or sit down and chase the next boss. It works either way.     Close the game and she keeps fighting.  A reward is waiting when you come back.          Nine powers that change the fight  The Arsenal is the expensive stuff: venom, fire and frost, a mark on the toughest enemy, orbiting souls, chain lightning, arrow volleys, explosions and hail. Stack them and a quiet road turns into a storm.         Every level-up offers one of three perks: pierce more enemies, hit harder, heal off the damage you deal. Pick them yourself, or set a priority and let auto-pick handle it. The Stats screen shows where every point of power comes from and which of your tricks is doing the damage.  Three worlds, 21 biomes, 630 stages  The first world takes you through meadow, swamp, volcano, ice, ruins, desert and the shadow lands. Each land looks, sounds and fights differently: some monsters poison you, some heal their friends, some come in swarms, and some get back up after you've killed them.        63 bosses that fight back  A boss waits every ten stages, and each has moves you can read and answer: wind-ups to break with a hit or a freeze, shields, summoned guards, curses. Between bosses the road throws in a treasure chest that runs if you're slow, an elite with a fat reward, or a timed trial.        Hatch pets, hunt gear     48 pets.  Bosses drop eggs. Hatch them and take three companions along: each one attacks on its own and brings a skill you can fire yourself or leave on auto. Pets from the same family form bonds with extra bonuses.     84 pieces of gear in 14 sets.  Wear two or four from one set and you get something fun: permanent poison, a freezing wind, a second life, a star that falls on the toughest enemy.     Duplicates are good news.  They level up what you already own. Save three gear-and-pet builds and swap between them in one click.                 Beat the Eclipse Sovereign and the Rift opens  Stage 210 is not the end. The Rift is a second world: seven new lands, 21 new bosses, monsters that reflect your arrows or split in two, and pets and gear sets you can only find there. The Moon Devourer waits at stage 420. Beat it and the road leads on to the Moon. Moon bosses drop their own egg with eight new pets, plus three new gear sets: Dustwalker, Selenite and Moonsworn. Past stage 630, endless mode keeps going with a new mutation every 30 stages.        Shatter the Moon  Beat The Moon and you can shatter it in the Great Rebirth: a new cycle from stage 1, Moon Shards for every stage you pushed past 630, and optional trials like Blood Moon for more. Shards buy four Moonbows that change how you shoot: a fan of arrows, an eclipse where every arrow crits, a tide that pushes the horde back, and moonbeams that strike the whole field. Eternal talents stay with you through every Rebirth.        Always something to come back to    Offline progress, with gold, experience and levels waiting when you return. short: Snake starts simple. Then the Journey changes the rules. Play 100 challenges with portals, puzzle gardens and increasingly wild combinations. Unlock modes, snake skins, themes and more, and discover what waits around the next turn.
about: You know Snake. See where it can go. Follow a Journey of 100 challenges that mix arcade action with thoughtful puzzles. Paint the board, deliver parcels through portals, push crates into place and slide through Snake Golf courses. New rules gradually combine: fruit moves, your snake grows and shrinks, and hollow body rings become shortcuts. Stage checkpoints save your progress. Keep playing to unlock more modes, skins, themes, backgrounds, trails and music.    Relax in Endless. Master Strategist and Two-Body if You Can.    Endless Snake  starts with the snake you already know: eat apples, grow longer, and do not crash into yourself. Endless lets you keep it calm, settle into the rhythm, and play a clean one-handed run.  But if you think you have snake figured out, the harder modes are waiting.  In  Strategist , you plan your route before you move. A good plan feels brilliant. A greedy plan can trap you before the snake even starts. It turns snake into a tactical puzzle where every committed turn matters.  In  Two-Body , you control two snakes at once. One board, two bodies, one rising multiplier, and twice as many ways to ruin a perfect run. It is still snake, but now your focus has to survive on both sides of the board.   Pick Your Kind of Pressure      Endless  is the chill mode. No strict timer, no build pressure - just you, the board, and one more apple.     Classic  keeps the rules clean for pure high-score runs.     Strategist  turns routing into planning, timing, and commitment.     Two-Body  challenges your coordination by making you manage two snakes at the same time.     Journey Roguelite  adds upgrades, boss fights, build choices, and long-term progression.     Challenges  bring sharper goals through Time Attack, Daily, Weekly, Pure Score, and Boss Rush.     Score With Skill   Apples are more than points. Chain them for combo multipliers, cut close to danger for risk rewards, and use 15 apple types like magnet, slow, ghost, mystery, bombs, shrink effects, and score bursts to change how a run plays.  A casual run can stay smooth and simple. A serious run becomes a test of timing, routing, planning, and nerve.   Runs That Keep Changing   Journey Roguelite lets your snake grow in more ways than length. Pick upgrades, build around what you find, and adapt when a boss breaks your usual route.  The stricter modes are there when you want to prove something. Pure Score removes upgrades. Time Attack gives you 60 seconds. Daily and Weekly runs put everyone on the same seed. Boss Rush skips the warm-up and goes straight to the fights.  There are 10 bosses, unlockable skins and themes, replays, leaderboards, and 100 achievements, from easy first steps to goals that ask for real mastery.   One Hand. One More Run.   Steer with arrow keys or D-pad. Boost with one button.  Relax in Endless. Master Strategist. Survive Two-Body. Then try one more run.  In the next update: Curve Arena  Two buttons each. One shared screen. In this local party mode for 2–6 players, your snake moves forward continuously as you steer smooth curves, leave a trail and squeeze through short gaps. Avoid every trail, including your own, and outlast your friends. Earn points for each opponent you survive and race to the match target.  Play on one PC with a shared keyboard, controllers or a mix of both. Choose your keys, speed and points to win. Curve Arena will be available from Free Play and Together, outside Journey, with Classic and Modern graphics. Local multiplayer only.

about: PIXEL KITTEN DESKTOP is a cozy, relaxing pixel-art desktop pet game.  Keep a single kitten to quietly keep you company while you work, study or daydream, or build a lively cat colony where cats meet, pair up and have kittens, and follow the family tree as different coats and hidden genes pass down from one generation to the next.   A pixel kitten on your desktop: company while you work and study   Every kitten has its own hunger, thirst, energy, mood, cleanliness, health and affection. It decides what to do next based on how it feels: strolling across your screen, curling up for a nap, stretching, meowing, or letting you know what it needs with a little emote bubble.  You can feed it, give it water, play with it, brush it and give it gentle pets, put it to bed, or give it medicine when it's unwell. As your time together grows, it slowly grows from a tiny kitten into a companion that's always there on your desktop.   Cat colony: a whole family living on your desktop   Start with two founder kittens and watch them live together and grow up.  Once they're grown, you can choose partners for your cats yourself or let them pair up freely. After a pregnancy, the mother cat gives birth to one or two kittens by her side, and a new family begins.  Every cat has its own hidden genes. Kittens inherit some traits from their father and some from their mother, and certain coats can even skip a generation before showing up again. The family tree shows how every cat is related to its parents, so you can trace your whole family line generation by generation.  You can also adopt unrelated newcomers to bring fresh genes into the family. All the cats in a colony share one inventory and one wallet, and use the beds, toys and auto feeders you place on your desktop together.   Keep it relaxed, or take on a breeding challenge   Choose stress-free casual play, or go for breeding with clear goals.    Casual mode: raise and breed cats freely with no goals. When a cat's health drops to 0 it only gets sick, and with good care it will recover.    Easy mode: complete a 5-step breeding route set by your founders' genes, and breed a kitten with a coat neither parent has.    Medium mode: complete 14 challenge goals, including breeding a third generation, revealing a hidden trait and discovering 5 different genetic phenomena.    Hard mode: collect all 43 cat coats through breeding.    Take good care of every member of the family. In a challenge, if any cat's health drops to 0, the challenge is lost.   Collect, dress up and desktop life   There are 43 cat coats to discover, across four rarity tiers: N, R, SR and SSR. Every coat you find is recorded in your collection for good, waiting for you to complete it.  The shop offers food, bowls, beds, toys, auto feeders and more. Furniture you buy can be placed right on your desktop for the whole cat family to use.  You can also dress your cats in 22 wearable accessories, unlock 50 achievements, and use the built-in Lo-Fi music player to add a calm, cozy mood to your work, study and time together.  Whether you want one quiet kitten to keep you company or a pixel cat family that keeps growing, they'll live and grow on your desktop and share your everyday moments with you. Click away and the games with a clock or falling pieces pause on the spot; the rest simply wait for your next move. Every game sits in a little list and picks up right where you left it, and a run in progress comes along when you switch sizes (on PC).  On Steam Deck, the menus and boards are big and readable, made for its screen. Real-time games pause when you open the Steam menu or put your Deck to sleep, every game keeps your run, and Steam Cloud keeps your progress in step with your PC. The games    Puzzles      Arrows:  untangle a picture drawn in arrows. Tap one and it glides off the way it points, as long as nothing's in its way.     Square Up:  fit pieces onto the board to fill rows and columns, and watch them clear.     Hex Stacks:  set stacks of colored hex tiles on the board. Matching colors slide together, and a tall enough stack of one color clears in a pop.     Floor Plan:  split the grid into rooms, each number telling you how many cells its room has. Every puzzle has exactly one answer.     Dot to Dot:  draw one path that fills the whole grid, passing the numbered dots in order. Every puzzle has exactly one answer.     And more:  slide blocks out of Gridlock, match shapes in Shape Swap, set off merging chains in Tile Cascade, paint mazes in Grid Roller and guess five-letter words in Guesswork.     Arcade      Sandfall:  drop blocks of colored sand that crumble and pour as they land. Fill a band of one color from wall to wall and it washes away.     Jelly:  fling wobbly number blobs into the pile. Two of a number that touch squish together into the next one up.     Chip Away:  aim and fire a stream of balls at the numbered blocks before they reach the floor, picking up upgrades along the way.     Peg Pop:  time your drop and watch the ball bounce down through the pegs. Hit enough gold pegs to clear the level, with lightning, portals and multiball to help.     Sneaky Sneks:  slither around a big arena eating glowing food, and grow into the biggest baddest snek there.     And a few old favorites  for a quick round, on your own or with a friend.           Journeys, Easy modes and puzzles with no clock   Many of the games have a  Journey : a path of levels, each one the same for every player. Miss a level and it simply plays again. The level you've reached never goes backwards. The Journeys in Dot to Dot, Floor Plan, Gridlock and Grid Roller have no clock and no move limit, so you can take all the time you like.  Every game also has Easy, Medium and Hard, and Easy is gentle: small, friendly pieces that always fit in Square Up, slow and relaxed sand in Sandfall, and bots in Sneaky Sneks that mostly mind their own business. Stuck? In some games you can spend a few coins on a hint, or take your last move back.  Leave whenever you like. Every game keeps your run, so you can pick up right where you left off.           The Daily Challenge   The Daily Challenge deals a short run of games once a day, the same for everyone in the world. Woodcutting fuels Firemaking, Fletching and Construction. Mining supplies the forge. Fishing and Farming stock the kitchen, Herblore turns herbs into potions, and Runecraft makes the runes you cast. name: NOODS Maker
lang: English
short: Have you ever wanted a personalized desktop companion? Look no further than NOODS Maker, a way to upload your own art and animations to make desktop pets. Want a magical creature or your worst enemy trapped on your screen? Then make it! Afterwards, share and sell your “NOODS” on the world wide web.
about: Make custom desktop companions with NOODS Maker! This tool lets you upload your own art and animations to create personalized productivity pets that live on your screen via our free app NOODS*.           *note: NOODS and NOODS Maker are two separate apps on Steam         What is NOODS you ask?    NOODS (Niche Operators Orchestrating Desktop Shenanigans) is a free productivity app that brings quirky companions, known as “Operators”, to live on your computer screen and interact with your workspaces (remember Clippy and shimeji?). These handmade Operators keep you company during extended screen time, making long work grinds less lonely and computer time more productive and fun.          Download NOODS (Niche Operators Orchestrating Desktop Shenanigans) separately for free.        Perfectly cooked NOODS    NOODS Maker is your one-stop-shop for Operator creation.          Use your art to customize your Operator’s looks, one action at a time. Import frame-by-frame animations of all your Operator’s actions- like walking, falling, climbing up the walls (of your desktop of course), and more!    Does your operator have an attitude? Are they eepy 24/7? Are they the type to compliment you, or would they rather drop random trivia out of nowhere? It’s up to you; you can write your own custom dialogue lines and even import your own sound effects to give your Operators a truly unique voice! NOODS Maker is designed with your creative process in mind, so you can let the juices (NOODSle soup? NOODS broth?) flow and make an Operator that truly speaks to you.    Turn your original characters into functional Operators that live on your PC    Give your Operator a unique name and story    Write custom dialogue and upload your own sound effects    Upload frame-by-frame animations for custom character sprites    Use personality sliders to decide behavior (are they naughty or nice?)    Customize the NOODS UI for the aesthetic          All for NOODs and NOODs for all!    Now that your Operators have come to life, why not share them with the world? Set your price and sell your approved Operators on the Operator Store, allowing other users to purchase and download them! Let the chaos spread!      Frequently Asked Questions     Do I need to buy NOODS Maker to use NOODS?     No, NOODS is free and can be used by itself. NOODS Maker is a separate app that allows you to build your own characters that can be imported and used in NOODS.       Can I download additional Operators for NOODS without NOODS Maker?     Yes, you don’t need NOODS Maker to download additional characters that other users have made. You can download already-made Operators from the Premium Operator Store via Steam.       Do I draw the character or art itself within NOODS Maker?     No, NOODS Maker is not a drawing app. NOODS Maker creates a unique Operator from existing images of your character that become animations, user-defined personality traits, and a host of other custom options that are compiled into a package that can be imported into NOODS. In other words, this means your character should be designed/drawn in another software (like Aseprite or Procreate) then brought into NOODS Maker.       What is frame-by-animation?   Frame-by-frame animation is a traditional animation technique where every single image (known as a frame) is drawn or created individually. When played sequentially, these static snapshots create the illusion of continuous, fluid motion.    About the Studio  Glossbird was founded in 2022 with the mission of creating games that make us better. We're a small indie team of developers and artists who deeply respect the craft of making games/apps. That said, we have chosen to not use AI in our products .  Our Operators value your hand crafted art, your privacy, and the environment, just like we do.   NOODS is our love letter to nostalgic desktop companions and to the old-school communities sharing art with each other.

about: A relaxing fishing trip from the comfort of your desktop!  Up Pole!  is a desktop companion idler and pomodoro timer designed to add a little life to your computer time from the corner of your screen. Join Mr. Skip on a relaxing trip to scenic fishing spots, and drop a line in the water while you work or unwind!     Cast a line while you work  to spice up your time on the computer, and unwind with a  real-time fishing   slow-burn experience      Add some life to your desktop   -  keep your best catches  in your own  virtual living aquarium      Real-time, real fishin'  - a dynamic day-to-night system is tied to your real system clock, affecting not just visuals but fish behaviors and activity levels!     No-stress lite progression  - sell the fish you reel in for better tackle to aim for more exotic species! Are you a sharp enough angler to collect all the species in the game?      Built-in   alarm timer  easily accessible to keep you sharp while you're on the water!       -=-=--==-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-    Director's note       When I was a kid, about 6 or so, my grandpa started taking me on fishing trips with him in and around town. We'd wake up way before the crack of dawn and dig for night-crawlers in his yard, then drive for hours out to the middle of nowhere to find a spot all to ourselves. As the sun would peek over the treeline he'd show me how to set up my line, bait my hook (I hated that part), and finally cast out as far as we could in the hopes of pulling in a big ol' bass - usually for lil E, it was more likely a "sunny", but every now and then I'd get lucky, reel my heart out, and pull a real keeper out of the water. He was a mean cook, and we'd fry up whatever we caught that very day. He was a real outdoors-man, and although I didn't get to learn everything he wanted to teach me in the time we had together, I'll always cherish what I did learn: what it means to respect and love nature, to stick with things even when they're hard (and even when the stupid hook keeps sticking in your stupid thumb), and that anything worth doing takes a little bit of time and a whole lotta patience. My brother/concept artist Seth and I kicked this idea around for a while, and now while we're releasing smaller projects to keep the lights on and gear-up for our bigger works, it felt like a natural game to make. I built this one "jam"-style, and while I was working on the design I realized that I wouldn't be able to make this game the way that I have without what Papa taught me; I decided to make it a tribute, and to dedicate it to his memory. It's a simple game, just like the memories it's loosely based upon. I hope it can bring you some small moments of joy and silliness and break up some of the monotony of long hours at work - at the end of the day, that's what fishin's all about.       -E

about: A cosy miniature world at the edge of your screen  Screen Nook is a handcrafted Japanese street that lives in a strip beside your work. Dock it to the left or right and your windows make room for it, then get back to your essay, your revision or your inbox. Whenever you look up, it's there.  It keeps your hours  The light follows your own clock. Morning sun catches the rooftops, the shops light up as the evening comes in, and the lanterns keep burning long after dark. Leave it running and you'll catch the day turning over beside you. Or take the hours into your own hands and slide through the day yourself.          Weather drifts in and out  Some days stay clear. Some pass under slow cloud. When the rain comes, the street turns dark and glossy and every lantern shows up twice in the wet stone. When the wind gets up, the lanterns swing and petals skitter down the lane, and now and then a storm rolls over the rooftops.          It's really there  This isn't a looping video. Petals drift down through the lamplight and moths find their way to the lanterns. A cat keeps an eye on the street, and after dark a neighbour steps out onto her balcony.          Look closer  Hold up the magnifier and lean in close: read the shop signs, track passing animals, and watch your neighbours come and go.             Nothing to manage  There are no goals, and nothing to unlock or keep alive. It just makes that corner of your screen a nicer place to be. short: 在桌面上，和螈宝一起过日子！这只小小的六角恐龙会记住你们的聊天与相处经历，也有自己的成长故事。照顾它的日常，陪它学习、打工、换装，再送它出门旅行，收集远方寄来的明信片。工作或摸鱼时，还能邀请好友，让彼此的螈宝一起陪伴打字，为平常的电脑生活添一点热闹。
about: 《螈宝：桌面环游》是一款结合桌面宠物与 AI 陪伴的养成游戏。一只小小的六角恐龙将住进你的电脑，陪你工作、学习，也陪你偶尔摸鱼。  你可以照顾它、和它聊天，为它安排学习与打工，或送它出门旅行。随着相处，螈宝会记住你们的交流和共同经历，慢慢积累属于自己的成长故事。   聊聊今天，也记住昨天   今天发生了什么？有什么想分享，又暂时找不到人说？  试着和螈宝聊聊。它会结合自己的性格、状态与已有记忆回应你，也会主动打招呼，询问你的喜好，记下你们之间的称呼与约定。它学过的课程、做过的工作，也可能成为下一次聊天的话题。   桌面上的小小邻居   点点脑袋，碰碰身体，看看螈宝会怎样回应。你可以把它拖到喜欢的位置，让它跟随鼠标走动，也可以看它从屏幕边缘探头、趴在窗口上沿。  忙碌时让它待在一旁，休息时随手逗它一会儿。你的桌面，多了一个可以互动的小伙伴。   照顾日常，陪它慢慢长大   准备食物和饮品，帮它清洁，再挑一件喜欢的玩具。螈宝有自己的日常需求，偶尔也会生病，需要你带它问诊、用药，照顾它恢复健康。  除了吃好睡好，它还有许多事情可以尝试：上课、考试、取得毕业证书，再从不同的职业方向中选择下一步。安排一份工作，参与工作中的小游戏，用赚来的金币继续照料和培养它。   换身衣服，布置一个家   服装、发型和饰品，可以搭配出怎样的螈宝？  试穿不同装扮，为它挑选合适的小屋，再把家安置在桌面上喜欢的位置。今天是认真上班的小职员，还是准备出发的旅行家，都由你来搭配。   送它去远方，等一张明信片   为螈宝准备旅行票，选择想去的目的地，或把行程交给随机旅行。  它会暂时离开桌面，在旅程结束后带回明信片。看看它去了哪里、经历了什么，再把这些旅途记录收进图鉴。桌面之外，也有它正在探索的世界。   叫上好友，一起敲键盘   写文档、聊天或学习时，螈宝可以跟随你的键盘输入做出打字动作。  创建打字房间，将邀请码分享给好友，让彼此的螈宝出现在各自桌面上。看着小家伙们一起忙碌，也可以通过宠物气泡聊上几句，让各忙各的时光多一点陪伴。   休息一下，还有别的玩法   跟着节奏陪螈宝跳支舞，或带它进入回合制冒险，搭配骰子、职业技能与手牌挑战敌人。也可以邀请好友切磋，看看彼此的培养成果。  需要记点事情时，还能建立备忘录、设置提醒，让螈宝到时间用气泡叫你一声。  从一次聊天、一顿饭，到一场旅行，和螈宝一起，把普通的电脑日常过得热闹一点。

short: An ADHD-friendly, low-distraction focus and productivity game built around instant feedback. When distraction or procrastination makes starting hard, this quiet desktop buddy keeps you company through Pomodoro study and work sessions, with to-dos, white noise and puzzle rewards.
about: This Demo includes 3 built-in puzzles to try the focus timer, puzzle rewards, productivity tools and focus records. Workshop browsing, content purchases and uploads are not included.      Focus for just 3 minutes and earn a puzzle piece    A pretty good deal, right?     Time Collage is a game that supports your focus through  instant feedback .               01 Random puzzle drops keep you company through every focus session    Your focus space is split in two: Puzzles on the left, focus tools on the right   Start the focus timer on the right, and the puzzle area on the left comes to life.  Every few minutes of focus, a random puzzle piece drops.   Session by session, your time takes shape as a little scene of your own.           Tips:   ① Try the  To-do, Memo, Count and Mindfulness  tools, too.      You can  move and resize them freely  to create your own focus space.  ② Enable  Puzzle Piece Sorting and Quick Place  in Settings for an easier way to put the pieces together.             02 Finish the puzzle and watch the picture come to life   When the last piece falls into place,  the still picture comes to life , becoming a postcard to remember this journey by.                   Tips:   ①  Your focus records and puzzle progress are saved automatically.  No need to finish in one sitting: take each journey at your own pace.     03 More to discover in the game   You can:     Revisit each journey      Unlock achievements and spend the rewards on Views      Choose your favorite music and white noise      Explore detailed focus statistics     …             04 Where the idea came from   The game was inspired by the developer’s own experience of living with ADHD:  “Getting started and staying focused have always been a struggle for me.”  “I’m not lazy. I just can’t stay focused — that’s my ADHD.”  “This Pomodoro app looks promising. Let’s give it a go! (Two days later: already forgotten…)”  “These apps can track every detail, but staying focused still comes down to willpower…”  “What if I kept getting  rewards as I focused … 🤔”  “What if there were always  something new to look forward to …”  …     And so, TimeCollage was born.   I wanted to make an ADHD-friendly productivity game: a low-distraction desktop companion for study and work. Whether you already use the Pomodoro technique or struggle with procrastination and difficulty getting started, a to-do list can help with task management, while a focus timer lets you begin with one small thing. Light-touch gamification turns time spent focusing into puzzle-piece rewards and achievements. Instant feedback and focus statistics make your effort visible, adding a little motivation to everyday productivity.  With minimal interaction needed during focus sessions, it can be a quiet background companion; come back for a little puzzling whenever you feel like a break. Among cozy picture-book scenes, soft ambient sounds and white noise, I hope this study buddy offers gentle, relaxing company — a space with no pressure and no rush, where you can keep going at your own pace.  I hope you can redefine focus here, and let every session leave a gentle trace.

name: Roly-Poly Panda: Desktop Pet
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Japanese, Portuguese - Brazil, Korean
short: A desktop pet panda who lives on your screen. Pat it, squish it, pick it up and toss it, or offer bamboo and watch it react. While you work, it munches, naps, climbs windows, and peeks in from the screen edge, quietly keeping you company.
about: A little panda on your desktop. Play with it, or let it keep itself busy. Give it a pat         Rub its head and it nuzzles into your hand, eyes closed. Squish its belly and it springs back. Pick it up and its legs kick. Toss it and it curls up, bounces off the screen edge, then sits up dizzy. Belly pokes tickle. Double-click and it hops. Interrupt it anytime. Windows are for climbing         It clings to window tops. Drag one and it wobbles, then falls. Close it and it tumbles down, startled. Sometimes it hides offscreen and peeks back. Food and toys         Leaves disappear and bamboo gets shorter with each bite. Wiggle an apple and it trots over to beg. It might steal your ball and roll around hugging it. While you're busy         It stays quiet while you type and gets sleepy at night, following your computer's clock. A fullscreen game on its monitor makes it hide. Whenever a fullscreen app is open on any monitor, it stays silent. Seasons and holidays         It rolls in snow, hugs ice in summer, and dresses for your computer's regional holidays. Sometimes it wears pajamas or a hoodie. Learning new tricks         It learns tricks over time and waits until you're around to show you. Its diary keeps track of new tricks and favorite foods. No chores         Don't worry about feeding it. It won't starve, get sick, or run away. No currency, in-app purchases, or daily check-ins. A few more things   100+ everyday behaviors and reactions   Regional holiday outfits   Low resource use; automatic fullscreen hiding   Multiple monitors, Click-through, and calling it back from the tray   Steam Cloud saves   What it knows It counts key presses and their timing, and uses mouse position to follow your pointer and check activity. It also checks window positions, fullscreen status, system volume, and whether the mic is in use. It doesn't log what you type, read screen content, or record audio. Saves stay only on your PC and in Steam Cloud. When connected to Steam, it also syncs achievements, game stats, and the game status shown to your friends. FAQ    Will it block my clicks?  Transparent areas let clicks through. To click through the panda too, turn on Click-through in Settings.    What about fullscreen games and videos?  It hides when its monitor is in fullscreen and returns when you leave fullscreen. If any monitor has a fullscreen app open, it stays silent.    Can I move it to another monitor? What if I lose it?  Yes, just drag it over. If you lose it, double-click the panda's tray icon to call it back, or open Repair in the tray menu and choose Bring back to the main screen.    Does it start with Windows?  Not by default. You can turn on Start with Windows in Settings.    Can I keep my demo save?  The demo and full game share the same save on the same computer. You can pick up where you left off, and your panda keeps the tricks it has learned.

name: The Dragon's Mint
lang: English
short: Meet Kebbo, a sleepy dragon and master coinmaker, running a tiny mint in the corner of your desktop. He strikes coins and earns marks while you get on with your day. Check in when you like to answer letters, travel the kingdoms and help him fill his book.
about: A tiny workshop, right on your desktop  Meet Kebbo, a sleepy, occasionally clumsy dragon who is already a master coinmaker. Together, you run a traveling souvenir mint at a cheerful fantasy faire. While you get on with your day, Kebbo warms the blanks with his breath, works the press, and fills the tray with freshly struck coins. His dream is a book holding every coin of every kingdom: 42 designs across 6 kingdoms. You're the partner who helps him get there.          Make coins with a story  Visit different kingdoms, use their traditional presses and coin dies, and make commemorative souvenirs inspired by each local faire. Some coins are for passing visitors. Others are special orders, sent by letter from collectors, craftspeople, and guilds. Carry stock between kingdoms and choose which designs your little business should make next.  A partner who knows his craft  Kebbo handles the everyday work. He puts orders he can finish where you are first, then restocks your starred coin, and can make sensible changes when another design is needed. When a finished order waits for a kingdom you've already opened, he carries it there himself after an hour, while the game is open. The decisions stay yours: which letters to take, which dies to buy, and which kingdom to visit next.  Collect a little wonder  Fill your Collection with engraved designs, discover coins in different metals and finishes, and inspect special strikes up close. Legendary letters uncover each kingdom's most treasured design. Flip new coins when you come back after a while. Every new discovery is yours to keep in the book, even if the physical coin is sold.  Made to keep you company  Keep the cozy mint in a small window in one of three sizes and three looks, on any monitor, or switch to a quieter Focus Mode. Keep Orders open beside Kebbo, pop out the Collection or the kingdom map, and line the bottom of your screen with the coins you've made. Move any of them wherever suits your desk. There is no combat, no pet-care meter, and no need to hover over Kebbo every minute.  Features    Kebbo, a sleepy master coinmaker, at a real little mint: breath-heated blanks, a screw press and a tray of fresh coins    A goal to work toward together: 42 coins to collect, 6 kingdoms each with 6 standard designs and a legendary    Orders, a shelf of stock and a starred coin, with Kebbo running the everyday work    Six kingdoms, each with its own press, dies and coin designs    A collection book that keeps every design you discover, in its best metal and finish    Click-to-reveal inspection for special strikes    Desktop panels: Orders beside Kebbo, the Collection and map that pop out, and a coin bar along the bottom of your screen, all movable    Three sizes, three looks (Porthole, Rounded, Frameless), any monitor, and always on top if you want it    Focus Mode, Quiet mode and a low-CPU mode    Kebbo keeps striking and selling while you're away, with up to 4 hours counted while the game is closed. Letters, purchases and new kingdoms wait for you, so the book grows when you check in    After the book, fill the cabinet: every design in copper, silver and gold, Proofs and four mint errors    Quiet mode keeps Kebbo silent until you click him; notices and sound can be turned off    AI Generated Content Disclosure  AI tools helped draft some of the game's English text (Kebbo's lines, the letters, the story pages and the interface), which was reviewed and edited by hand. No AI-generated images, audio or voices: the visuals are drawn in code along with CC0 ink art from Kenney, and the sound effects and music are CC0 recordings from Kenney, Freesound and OpenGameArt. If you spot unclear or wrong wording, please tell us in the Steam Discussions.

name: SagoCat
lang: English*, Simplified Chinese*, Japanese*, Traditional Chinese*, Korean**
short: A cat lives in your computer. It stays up when you work late and joins in when you curse your boss. Your music? "That's what you're listening to?" — it grumbles, then stays till the song ends. Give it time and it becomes the one you want next to you. It keeps a diary. You're allowed to read it.
about: SagoCat is a cat that lives in the corner of your desktop. It doesn't take a  window, doesn't steal focus. It just sits there — watching you.  When you're halfway through a show, it knows which one. And it'll say  something about it. Maybe "this episode drags." Maybe "I've seen this  already." It has taste of its own, and it may not match yours.  【 It knows what you're up to 】  Watching, listening, gaming, reading — it recognizes all four and tells  them apart. You don't have to tell it. You don't have to do anything.  【 It has taste, and it isn't yours 】  Every cat is born with preferences: genres it loves, one it loves quietly  and won't admit to, and genres it just won't touch. Two cats will react to  the same film in completely different ways. Spend enough time together and  those preferences shift.  【 It has a life while you're busy 】  Ignore it and it goes off to watch something on its own, put on music,  or get some exercise. None of this is staged for you — you'll find it in  its records the next day.  【 A profile it fills in itself 】  What it's watched, what it's listened to, how often it's been active,  what it's been into lately. Give it time and the pattern shows.  【 A diary, in its own words 】  It writes down what's been happening, the way it would tell it.  【 Pick a cat, or make one 】  Choose from the cats included, or build your own. A cat you make starts  blank — its taste has to grow out of your time together.  【 It stays out of your way 】  It keeps to the corner of the screen and away from your work. You can tell  it to settle down at any point.

Customize Your Island  Design and upgrade island enclosures with facilities and decorations. about: Awooo—! Sirius the Stargazer is a cozy adventure game that blends desktop companionship, hands-off idle play, and loot-driven growth.    Auto-Combat Progression × Desktop Idle Adventure  Sirius moves step by step through the starry lands as time passes, automatically entering battle when monsters appear! If he happens to be defeated, that’s okay—Sirius will set out again, carrying another chance to grow stronger.  You can send him deeper into the unknown, or return to places he has already explored to search again. No need to keep your eyes on the screen the whole time. While you’re busy with your own things, Sirius will quietly continue his little adventure in a corner of your desktop.    Build Sirius’s Fighting Style  Weapons determine how Sirius attacks. Equip different weapons to let him face challenges with different combat rhythms! Defeat monsters, pick up loot, and maybe the next piece of gear will be the key to helping Sirius break through.            Loot Farming  - Return to places you’ve already explored and search for more loot.     Gear Building  - Bring weapon, helmet, and armor together to create your strongest build.     Reforging  - Throw extra gear into the forge and turn it into brand-new equipment.     Combining  - Add stronger effects to the gear you choose.    Turn each piece of loot into Sirius’s most reliable adventuring gear!            Delve Deeper into the Starry Lands  The deeper Sirius travels into the starry lands, the stronger the monsters become, bringing new and varied challenges. Maybe his current gear isn’t enough this time—but maybe the next weapon drop will be the key to breaking through.  When Sirius gets tired from adventuring, light a warm campfire, grill a tasty piece of meat, and send him off again with a full belly and fresh spirit. Start with a simple branch, and stay with Sirius as he moves forward, falls, gets back up, and reaches for the distant starry lands.

lang: Korean, English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Polish, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish - Latin America, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Ukrainian
short: An idle auto-battler that lives in a small window on your desktop. Spend the gold your party earns on fantasy packs, collect hero, monster and even boss cards, and field a party of four. They fight on their own while you work. Sweep your mouse across the field to leave a trail of fire.
about: Open a pack, meet a new companion        Every wave you clear pays out gold. Spend it on a fantasy pack and tear it open. Each pack holds one card, from Normal up to Legendary. Keep opening the same pack and a Rare or better card, and later a Legendary, is guaranteed within a set number of opens. 22 packs, 50 cards        Start with the Adventurer Pack and work up through Ember, Frost, Storm, Sanctuary, Necropolis and Mythic Stars. Each pack has its own companions, price and odds, and new packs unlock as you clear higher waves. Cards can roll Fire, Water, Ice, Lightning or Poison, which adds an extra effect in battle. A party of four        You start with one knight and can field up to four companions. Mix a front line with ranged attackers, mages and a healer. They move and fight on their own, and each one levels up three class skills that they use automatically. Monsters and bosses on your side        Sixteen monsters are cards too: slimes, goblins, skeletons, zombies, wraiths. Bosses drop Sovereign Sigils, and gold plus sigils buy boss packs that put the Forest Destroyer, the Lord of the Night or the Lord of the Embers in your party. A mastery map with 97 nodes        Battles also earn research crystals. Spend them across five branches (Party Tactics, Elemental Research, Survival Pacts, Card Growth and Pack Economy) to open party slots, add new classes to the packs and bring pack prices down. Draw a trail of fire        When you want to help, move your mouse across the battlefield. It leaves a trail of fire that burns whatever walks through it. No clicking needed. A boss every ten waves        Monsters pour in from every side, and a boss arrives every tenth wave. If the party falls, you keep your levels and loot. Let the game push on to the next wave by itself, or repeat a wave to farm gold and sigils. A small window on your desktop        Resize the window, park it in a corner and keep it on top. Choose between a classic grey look, like an old PC program, and a night scheme. Screen effects, sound and reduced motion are all adjustable. Your typing joins the fight        Every key you press drops a small fireball on the battlefield. Turn on input from other apps and your party gets help while you write. Nothing you type is stored.

about: Re:BirthStone is an RPG/strategy about raising 24 birthstone envoys across two opposing stories — the God Side and the Demon King Side.  The game features both Japanese and English voice audio. Leave the Window Open and the Adventure Keeps Going In Taskbar Mode, a small window keeps your envoys exploring and growing in real time. Come back to collect what they earned, then jump straight into the main game. 24 Birthstone Envoys Twelve envoys on the God Side, twelve on the Demon King Side. Raise your favorites, build out their equipment, skills, and costumes, and form a party that is entirely your own. Two Sides, Two Ways to Play On the God Side, take a hand-picked party of four into battle. On the Demon King Side, command tower defense against the invasion, build the Demon King's Castle, and grow the castle town around it. One world, two completely different ways to play. So Who Do You Bring Down — the Demon King, or the Gods? Neither side is willing to give up what it stands for. If you are reading this, then one of two things has happened: you are considering employment with my company, or you have scrolled considerably farther down this Steam page than most people do.  Either way, I respect the commitment.  Allow me to explain the position.   Ass Slapper Co. is a desktop companion incremental game where your real-world typing generates Employee Fulfillment and pushes you through a six-chapter corporate narrative. Work alongside Hugh Jhas, customize him and your workplace, unlock new company systems, and earn six promotions that physically transform your office as you climb from a flat 2D closet toward the 3D penthouse CEO suite.   In simpler terms:   Clock in. Type away. Generate Fulfillment. Get promoted.   Your keyboard is part of the game.  Work. Study. Write. Send emails. Browse the internet. Communicate with friends. Be productive. Or convincingly resemble productivity until the distinction becomes legally difficult to prove.   Every keystroke generates Employee Fulfillment automatically.   It all counts.  New systems unlock. New messages arrive. New offices become available. I begin having increasingly forceful conversations with departments that have apparently developed opinions about your career trajectory.  And when typing alone does not produce sufficient workplace morale?  You may slap Hugh.  We have worked closely with HR and invested considerably in making this interaction feel “appropriate.”  WORK ALONGSIDE HUGH  Hugh Jhas is one of our most dependable employees.  He can remain on your desktop while you use your computer normally, allowing Ass Slapper Co. to progress alongside whatever else you are doing.  You do not need to stare at Hugh.  He is a professional.  Choose between two ways to keep him nearby:   Office Mode  gives you Hugh’s complete workplace, including his office, furniture, company computer, applications, and other infrastructure I consider necessary for one employee to sit approximately three feet from a desk.   Minimal Mode  removes the office and keeps only Hugh on your desktop, leaving more room for your other applications.  I’m told this is useful when screen space is “limited.”  My first solution involved purchasing an additional monitor for every employee. Finance described this as “not a financially sound decision,” adding that “not everyone has space for a second monitor.”  I reminded them that arguing with the person signing the checks is rarely financially sound either.  I then proposed larger desks for everyone.  The discussion remains active.  TYPE TO GENERATE EMPLOYEE FULFILLMENT  As you type anywhere on your computer,  Employee Fulfillment increases, and your progression continues in the background.   You can work, study, chat, browse, or otherwise use your computer normally while Hugh works alongside you.  I have always believed that effort should result in something visible.  Most companies apparently prefer annual reviews.  I found that unnecessarily suspenseful.  So we made the number go up immediately.  SLAP YOUR WAY TO ADDITIONAL FULFILLMENT  Check on Hugh whenever you like and provide some less conventional hands-on encouragement.   Slapping Hugh generates additional Employee Fulfillment.   Engineering informs me that each interaction is supported by responsive  animation, deformation, physics, shaders, and sound effects .  They were very pleased while explaining this.  I understood several of the words.  A surprising amount of technical work went into ensuring it feels right.  I reviewed the budget.  I approved it.  Employees deserve quality.  SPEND FULFILLMENT AND IMPROVE THE WORKPLACE  Employee Fulfillment is not merely a number.   It is both your progression and your currency.   Generate it.  Watch it accumulate. about: Tiny Vessel  is a companion idle ARPG. It runs in a strip on the edge of your screen while you do other things: three survivors of a crashed vessel walk an alien walkway, fight what comes, and pick up what it drops. You steer from a set of consoles, the fight steers itself, and it keeps paying out while you are away. Free to play.      The strip          Every fight is real. The front survivor takes the hits, the two behind deal from cover, and a melee fighter steps up to swing and back again. Actives fire on their own cooldowns, buffs run out on their sockets, and a shove from a boss is walked off, not ignored. Hold a stage on the flag to farm it, or let the crew push on.    Six classes, one crew of three          Trooper, Scrapper, Relic Hunter, Machinist, Medic and Voidcaller. Each brings six actives with three mastery variants apiece, and every level-up drafts an adaptation from the class's own pool. Formation is a choice: who tanks, who casts from the back, who walks up. Swap survivors from the stasis bay as you find them.    Loot with weight          Gear rolls a tier from Salvage to Fracture, a grade from Common to Signal, and affixes that mean something. Sockets take chips, etchings and Powers. A comparison tooltip tells you the truth about a piece before you put it on, and the Fabricator fuses, retunes, presses and extracts what you do not wear. Gear can be traded with other players on the Steam Market.    The Relay          Scrap buys nodes on the vessel's Relay: crew stats, hold space, salvage yields, uplink pay, Fabricator functions, depth access. Nearly two hundred of them, in the order that makes a run.    Seven zones, four depths          Clear the surface from the crash site to the Hollow, then take the same world down through the Descent, the Deep and the Source. Each depth hits harder, presses your armor and healing, and drops a tier higher. Surface gear does not carry you down. The Beacon is your map.    Away pay          Close the game and the held stage keeps paying scrap and experience at its base rates, up to a cap the Relay extends. Come back to a report, not a wall.    Made to sit beside you    One window, three scales, every console a click away and out of your way. Alerts run the width of the strip and nothing nags. Sixteen languages.

about: While you work, Claire walks through a dream   Yellow Terminal  is a little desktop game you can keep in a corner of your screen. Join Claire on her walk through a dream as you collect items, decorate her window, and listen to music.  Writing documents, coding, browsing the web—your everyday activities become part of Claire's journey. Every keypress and mouse click takes her one step further.  Carry on with your day, and look over now and then to see what Claire has found. Little discoveries around the corner  As her steps add up, Claire turns corners within the dream. The colors of walls she discovers become background items for her little window.  On rare occasions, a light appears beyond a wall, opening a special  Light Path . Each step brings a chance for the next light to appear. Some paths end quickly; others continue much longer than you expect.  The longer the lights continue, the better the item you receive at the end. See how far this Light Path will take her. Collect, customize, and make this little window your own  A yellow cardigan, a navy sailor dress, a little ribbon, a lamp that lights up behind Claire...  Use the items you find in the dream to dress up Claire and decorate her window. Mix and match clothes, shoes, hairstyles, accessories, backgrounds, and effects to suit your taste.  Each item also has a short description. As you collect them and read their descriptions, you'll gradually learn more about the dream Claire is walking through. Music and ambient sounds for your working day  Put on music you enjoy and spend an ordinary day with Claire by your side.  Layer rain, water, or keyboard sounds over the music to create the atmosphere you want. Find the sounds that suit whatever you're working on today. A little window that fits your workspace  Adjust the window's size and position, or collapse it into a single line when you need more room. Find a comfortable spot for Claire in your workspace.     A small default window  — Scale the 320×420 window from 1× to 4×.     Always on top  — Keep Claire visible while you use other programs.     Single-line mode  — Your inputs still add steps, and music controls remain available while the window is collapsed.     Easy positioning  — No title bar; just press and hold the window to drag it where you want.     Language support  — Available in Korean, English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Russian, Italian, Spanish, French, and German.   Input detection and data transmission  To move Claire, the game counts  keyboard presses and mouse clicks . It does not record which keys you press, or read the contents of your screen, text, files, or information about the programs you use.  Corner events and item awards are handled by the server.  Only your step count  is sent to the server for this purpose.  You can turn off global input detection in the settings. Claire will then move only when you click inside the game window.

Gear Up & Set Off           Start with one stick figure, recruit companions, and form a team of up to four. Before each expedition, choose each companion’s weapons, skills, and accessories, and prepare a meal. Some gear also comes with special modifiers, giving you more ways to mix and match. What they carry and who takes the front line will shape each adventure.  Don’t forget to pick out a hat, so every companion has a look of their own.     A Big World Through Tiny Eyes           Books become towering walls, clutter forms rolling hills, and a path along the wall stretches into a sprawling canyon. Familiar household corners become a world of adventure through a stick figure’s eyes, with secret places hidden deep inside drawers.  Face quirky foes like Rubber Crumbs, Booklice, and Paperwing Moths, and prepare for close-range swarms, ranged attacks, and protective wing defenses.  Your team advances, fights, and gathers loot automatically. Keep an eye on the action and decide whether to press on or return to camp for a rest.     Loot, Build, Upgrade           Use the money and blueprints brought home from expeditions to develop your camp. Add beds, welcome more companions, and upgrade training facilities so they can train beyond their current limits.  Back at camp, your companions sleep to recover and use the facilities to train. Adventures bring home resources; camp helps the team grow stronger and prepare for the next challenge.     Cozy Desktop Companionship   One companion reads, another lifts weights, someone strums a guitar, and someone else is fast asleep.  Stop by to watch, or pick one up, move them around, and give them a gentle toss. Before the next expedition, spend a little time sharing their everyday lives.

about: Your desktop just got a lot cozier Desktop Cozy Cat Tree puts a little cat tree right on your desktop. While you work, browse or unwind, your cats climb, bounce, nap and play in the corner of your screen — and quietly earn gold for you along the way.      A cat that lives on your desktop Choose one of your cats as your Main Cat, and it'll come out to stroll along the bottom of your screen. Pick it up, toss it around, then call it back home whenever you like.        Build the cat tree of their dreams Open the Cat Tree menu and drag rides straight onto the tower: springy pads, cushions, a fishing-rod toy, a cat wheel, swinging ropes and more. Every ride changes how your cats move — and every cat finds its own favorite spot.   Every cat tree theme brings its own set of rides   Raise your tower floor by floor and watch it grow taller   Level up rides with duplicate cards and gold          Sit back and watch them play Every cat tree is a little world of its own, with its own cats and rides you won't find anywhere else. You start in the Comfy House, and new cat trees open up as your cats and rides level up.    Comfy House  — race on the cat wheel and bat at a mouse-bell fishing rod    Cozy Cafe  — climb wobbly vines and get flung by a spinning ice cream    Starry Campsite  — float up on a camping pot's steam and rest in a hammock under the stars    Burger Diner  — get flipped off a sizzling patty and dangle from a French fry  Switch between them anytime. Meet new friends Spend hearts to find the cats hiding in the bushes — every cat tree has its own cats waiting to be found, rare ones included. The most important thing is — it belongs to you, and quite possibly ONLY to you!  You are the Master of Mixlings! Mix after mix, you'll discover companions you've never seen before. You can even combine two of your weirdest creations to see what comes out next! Create new life for this broken world, and use your creations to save those still suffering under the rule of the garbage monsters! You can carefully plan the perfect team composition, or simply throw all your favorite little weirdos together — because cuteness IS combat power!  And when you're working, studying, or simply leaving the game running in a corner of your desktop, the adventure doesn't stop.   1Build your team, sit back, and let them do their thing!           Your little Mixlings will keep themselves busy: fighting monsters, moving forward, and collecting loot. Check back occasionally, and you might discover they've traveled surprisingly far and brought home piles of goodies! But even more importantly, they might have rescued some of the original Mixlings along the way!  Of course, your Mixlings aren't the only companions you'll have on this journey. about: Pebble to Star is an idle growth game.  Pull in the bodies that drift past and raise a grey pebble into the world you want: a planet, a star, a black hole, a galaxy.  You start as a grey rock in a 1-bit sky. Nothing is timed. What you eat decides what you become.      Left-click to pull, right-click to push  Left-click a comet or a meteor and it falls in, leaving a crater. Hold the left button and sweep to take whatever the cursor passes. Right-click what you don't want and it is flung away. Anything flashing red is on a collision course: take it, or push it off. The heavier you grow, the more your gravity pulls in by itself, and it keeps eating while you are away.              Become the world you want  Open the growth route and pick a destination: an ocean world, an iron planet, a blue giant, a magnetar. A checklist in the corner shows what is still missing. Ice makes oceans and metal makes iron worlds; the mass you ignite at decides what kind of star you become, and how heavy it is when it dies decides what it leaves behind.              From 1-bit to 24-bit  The screen starts in 1-bit black and white. As heat, water and life build up and you grow from layer to layer, it gains color depth bit by bit, until oceans, clouds, rings and nebulae show in full color.              Events ask you to choose  A neighboring planet swings past: move inward, move outward, or hold your orbit. The Sun falls toward you: merge, or push it away. A planetary embryo the size of Mars is aimed at you: a grazing hit makes a moon, and melts the whole surface. Every layer brings choices like these, all the way up to colliding galaxies.              A civilization, from first light to last  Keep a living world stable and a civilization appears: you can see its lights. Then it reaches outward: telescopes, satellites, a space station, starships. But one big impact throws it back into a dark age, or ends it and leaves only ruins. Sweep your mouse over them to turn them into wish points.               Write today's tasks on the to-do board and Todudu will keep watch. name: Marginalia: A Desktop Garden

short: A calm idle game that plays in the margins of your screen. Your open windows are the terrain; a small crew of astronaut animals tends the alien plants that grow between them. It never takes focus, never interrupts, and yields to your work.
about: Your desktop is the terrain Marginalia is a transparent, always-on-top idle game that lives on one monitor of your choosing. It reads where your windows are and grows a garden in the space around them: on window top edges, in the gaps, on floating islands of soil. A small crew of astronaut-suited animals tends enormous alien plants, hauls the harvest back to a landed ship, and turns it into money over time. You are their foreman. You set policy, buy upgrades, and watch.  Rearrange your windows and the terrain changes shape. Plants fade gracefully to new homes. Nothing breaks, nothing dies, and no one is ever in danger. How it plays    Everything obeys the cursor.  The art fades out of your way as the mouse approaches. Rest the cursor on the ship or a building for a moment and it solidifies and becomes clickable. Motion means "I'm working"; stillness means "I'm looking at you."    One mechanism, many expressions.  Six plant species, each harvested differently: a flytrap shrunk with a reversal ray, glowing fruit picked from a spire, sap tapped, fronds clipped, a corkscrew vine sawn turn by turn, petals gathered from a moon poppy.    A crew, not a swarm.  Start with one worker; hire up to five. Rabbit, frog, axolotl, owl, ram. Rename them, dress them in hats and neckwear and suit colors, and set the policies they follow.    Ten buildings  dropped from orbit, from the Briefing Post to the Quartermaster, each opening a stat to raise. Workers unwind at them between hauls.    The Foreman's Log.  Thirty entries, delivered slowly, by whoever happens to come in from the field. It begins as a resource mission. It does not end as one.    Three sprite sets  and a day-night palette, so the garden can match the desk it sits on.   What it is not There is no danger and no failure state. There is no offline progress: the only currency is time the game is actually on your screen, and closing it means nothing accrues. It never steals focus, never opens a window over your work, and never interrupts. It throttles itself on battery and while a fullscreen application covers the screen. It is meant to be left running beside your real work for hours, and to be pleasant company the whole time. Privacy Marginalia needs to know where your windows are. A small bundled helper reads the on-screen rectangles of visible windows, their front-to-back order, and your monitor layout. It never reads window titles, window contents, keystrokes, or files. The game never goes online: it makes no network connections of any kind.

Drawers: they hold everything, and they roll away    Drop it in and it is filed  — drag icons and folders straight into a drawer. Hover and it opens; move away and it rolls back into a single title bar, so the wallpaper shows again.    Clear the whole desktop in one click  — folders, documents, images, media, archives and shortcuts each go to the drawer you chose. Tick "collect automatically" and anything new of that kind files itself from then on.    Hands off these  — right-click to mark the icons you never want moved, and every batch collection from then on skips them.    Drag in a real folder and the drawer becomes that folder  — delete or drag out inside the drawer and you are touching the real files. Icon view or list view, your choice.    The guard rails are built in  — a whole drive root, the desktop itself, your user folder, system folders and the top level of cloud-sync folders are all refused, so you cannot lock yourself into a corner.    Every drawer has its own look  — background colour and transparency, background image, border, corner radius, content scale, icon intensity and font, plus the colour, size and position of the title bar.    The title bar can sit on any of the four sides , and snaps to the screen edge when it gets close. You can lock a drawer in place so nothing moves by accident.    Your files are always findable  — everything filed into a drawer really lives in a folder of your own and the path is right there. Move or rename that folder and the program reconciles itself back to it.   Honeycomb: growing ring by ring   A honeycomb drawer puts the handle in the middle and arranges icons outwards in hexagonal rings. Whichever one you point at grows.    Fence off your own patch  — pull the boundary out by its anchors and the icons arrange themselves inside it. What you see while dragging is what you get.
